heroHeadline: Sisi Hosts Saudi Crown Prince on Red Sea Security, Then Abbas as Egypt Rejects Palestinian Displacement Amid Gaza Escalation Fears
heroSubtitle: President Abdel Fattah el-Sisi hosted Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman in Cairo on September 15, 2026, with both leaders stressing the need for secure navigation in the Bab el-Mandeb Strait and Red Sea after Houthi attacks injured 73 people across southern Saudi Arabia and a drone strike forced a temporary shutdown of the East-West oil pipeline; they called Saudi and Egyptian security 'inseparable' and agreed to accelerate trade and investment ties, with bilateral trade up ~20% to $7.1 billion in H1 2026. On September 16, Sisi received Palestinian Authority President Mahmoud Abbas in Cairo, reiterating Egypt's rejection of Palestinian displacement — hours after Israeli Defence Minister Israel Katz said the army would 'finish the job' in Gaza — and pledging continued mediation to implement the October 2025 Sharm El-Sheikh ceasefire agreement. Separately, the Central Bank of Egypt held its policy rate at 19% for a fourth straight meeting on August 20 as inflation stayed elevated at 14.9%, while the Suez Canal Economic Zone drew a record $7.26 billion in contracted investment across 117 projects for FY2025/26.
footerNote: Data sourced from Egyptian official records, UNESCO, academic Egyptology research (Shaw, Lehner, Hawass), major international outlets, IMF, Human Rights Watch, and institutional analyses.
